pages.text:
A reactor fails the way a real one does, and always warns first: alarms on the Safety page of its screen, on Jade, and a klaxon. Silence stops the klaxon until a new alarm sounds.
# Cladding failure
Above about 1,200 °C the Zircaloy cladding reacts with steam. It makes Hydrogen and lets fission products into the coolant: the coolant, and the containment's air, turn radioactive.

# Hydrogen
Hydrogen builds up in the containment's air. Above 4% a spark or heat source (fire, lava, a torch, a lit machine, Corium) ignites it in an explosion. Hydrogen Recombiners remove it without a flame.
# Meltdown
Above about 2,800 °C the fuel melts into Corium: a glowing, intensely radioactive molten fluid. It melts down through blocks, but not obsidian, Containment Concrete or a Core Catcher, and slowly cools (faster beside water) into Solidified Corium, still radioactive.

# Overpressure
Past the vessel's limit (130% of its design pressure) a steam explosion ruptures it. Relief Valves vent steam first.
# Prompt-critical excursion
If reactivity jumps past prompt critical with nothing to stop it, power spikes in seconds and the explosion destroys the vessel.
# Explosions
Their size grows with the energy and pressure stored, up to a cap in the config. Explosions, meltdowns and fallout can each be kept from damaging blocks in the config.
